emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(dev->reg_state)]) from thread_b (the sysfs read of the lifecycle state must not interleave with a conflicting write)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: thread_b reads reg_state holding dev_base_lock (via netdev_show), but in the buggy version thread_a writes reg_state holding only RTNL and NOT dev_base_lock; the two protections are DIFFERENT locks, so same_lock(read,write) is false and no shared lock serializes them → no g establishes atomic(read)
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic over a single access; a read and a conflicting write guarded by non-matching locks are effectively unsynchronized → data race

fix_maps_to: register_netdevice (and netdev_run_todo, unregister_netdevice_many) now wrap the dev->reg_state writes in write_lock(&dev_base_lock) → the writer and the sysfs reader share dev_base_lock → serialize(dev_base_lock, [reg_state write]) now MATCHES the reader's lock → establishes atomic(read)
recall_risk_notes: Good fit for the contract's keep/reject + same_lock arbitration: both sides take SOME lock, but different ones (RTNL writer vs dev_base_lock reader). Recall hinges on the model NOT being fooled by 'both sides are locked' — it must recognize the locks differ (the sound same_lock grounding helps here). Risk: an LLM may judge the writer's RTNL sufficient and reject the race (FN). Object/threads are static-friendly (well-known register/sysfs ops on one struct field; surface pre-fills reg_state + both candidate locks). Benign 1-byte state-flag tearing race in practice.
